summary: Carl W. Ernst is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned an A.B. at Stanford and a Ph.D. at Harvard. He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as Kenan Distinguished Professor at UNC-Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a linguistics and archaeology scholar. He studied at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen (under Wilamowitz-Moellendorff and Leo), and Berlin. He was a professor of Greek language and literature at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

Carl William Belser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Michigan and earned his Ph.D. under Friedrich Delitzsch at Leipzig (1887–1889). Belser later taught at Michigan (1889, 1891) and headed Latin at Colorado Boulder (1893).

Carl von Noorden was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Bonn, Paris, and Berlin, learning under Martin Haug and Leopold von Ranke. He was a history professor at Greifswald, Marburg, Tübingen, Bonn, and Leipzig (1877).

Carl-Martin Edsman was a religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala University (~1930–1940), the University of Paris (~1937–1938), and Lund University (~1940–1944). He held posts at Lund University (~1940–1944) and Uppsala University (~1950–1977).

Carlo Bernheimer was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Bologna (~1897–1901) under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè. He served as a Docent of Sanskrit at Bologna from 1906 to 1938 and held a post there in 1945.
Carlo Della Casa was an Indologist who studied under Mario Vallauri at the University of Turin from ~1945 to 1949. He later held a post at the University of Palermo from ~1964 to 1969.

Carlo Formichi was an Indologist who studied at Naples, Vienna under Bühler, and Kiel under Deussen and Oldenberg. He held professorships in Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898–1905) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Turin, Pisa, SNS Pisa, and under Weber, Spiegel, Roth, and Ascoli. He served as professor of Latin literature at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1874–1900).
Carlo Jamelle Harris is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carlo Puini was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Pisa. In 1877, he became an extraordinary professor of East Asian history and geography at the University of Florence.

Carlo Salvioni was a linguistics scholar who studied at Basel and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Karl Brugmann). He served as a professor at the University of Pavia (1890–1902) and the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1902).

Carlos Garcia-Jane is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Barcelona, Aberystwyth, South Wales, and Edinburgh (PhD 2022). His posts include librarian at RCSSD (2022), indexer at Indexing Craft (2023), and reviews editor for Buddhist Studies Review (2023).
Carlos Lopez is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Michael Witzel. He held positions at Harvard University (attested 1994–2000) and Florida State University (attested 2000).

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religion who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio, and under Shigeru Gorai. She served as Lecturer in Japanese at Cambridge (from 1958) and president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires and served as vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1988–2018).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001. She was a research fellow at Hamburg (attested 2008) and joined Ruhr University Bochum's CERES in 2013.

Carol A. Breckenridge was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976). She held an academic post at the University of Chicago from ~1990 to 1999.

Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carol Salomon was an Indologist who completed degrees at City College of New York (~1966–1970) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1983, PhD). She served as Senior Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Washington.
